description: Where each part's box sits on the map's coarse grid, [column, row]. Everything else the map draws -- box sizes, pin sides, districts, outlines, routes and bundles -- is computed from the model (apps/viewer/map.js; docs/DAG_TOPOLOGY.md, "The map"). The map is a second drawing of the same model, never a second model.

provenance.arrangement: Tall, after Jeff's sketch of 2026-11-10 (Jeff, 2026-11-17: the one arrangement is portrait, so it fits the Side by side region): seven columns by ten rows. The base body is the left column read upward as the hardware stacks -- hub, tangential link mount, gas-spring mount, piston cover -- and the pitch plate body's column of the piston and its heads the sixth, in the same sense -- plate, piston body, lower head, upper head -- so the end-stop route runs across the top and the feather stop and the slide cross under it. Since 2026-11-22 (Jeff's note 20261122T211136_iubdsx: line the lug stacks up, draw each link as a two-force member in a row, fewer crossings) each link is five boxes in one line: the tangential link a row from the mount end's inner race, beside the mount in the base column, to the plate end's inner race under its bolt; the pitch link a column down the seventh from the plate end's inner race to the pitch arm end's, at the end of the blade's row -- hub, blade root, pitch arm, that inner race. Each lug stack is a column -- inner race, bolt, flanged bushing -- with the plate beside the flanged bushing at the top, the tangential link's in the fifth column, the pitch link's in the seventh; 215177-001's outline is that row of three. The plate has room beside it for four parts and five meet it (the piston body and four bushings), so the straight bushings sit in the plate's column under it: the tangential link's straight under the plate, beside its bolt (the stack's second load path, plate -- straight bushing -- bolt, a square with the first), the pitch link's between the two plate-end inner races, beside its own. A straight line from every inner race to its plate cannot be had while each body is one rectangle: a race at the end of its lug's line sits inside the pitch plate's district, so its link must leave that rectangle from a corner, and the gas-spring mount must meet the piston, which pins the plate's rectangle to the base's side -- the lesson of the handoff above shows the search. Placed by scoring candidates with the map's own notes, crossings included (tests/debug_map_arrangement.mjs): this one has no note, no route crosses another, and its bounds are the same as the arrangement before it.
